Header.cap: Logo and menu strip at the very top
Header.desc: The same strip at the top of every page. Usually holds the logo, menu, and a signup button.

Navbar / GNB.cap: The menu part inside the header
Navbar / GNB.desc: The menu for moving between pages. In Korea it's also called the GNB (Global Navigation Bar).

Hero.cap: First screen's big headline and button
Hero.desc: The first thing visitors see. Says what the site does in one line and offers a single button.

Sidebar.cap: Vertical menu panel along the side
Sidebar.desc: A menu column pinned to one side of the screen. Common in admin dashboards and docs sites.

Footer.cap: Info strip at the very bottom
Footer.desc: The bottom area for less-urgent stuff like company info, terms, and contact details.

Layout.cap: Where header, sidebar, body, footer go
Layout.desc: The skeleton that decides where the big areas of a screen go. Layout first, content second.

Section.cap: One of the chunks a page is split into
Section.desc: A big chunk of the page on one topic. You can just say "add a reviews section."

Container.desc: Keeps content centered so it doesn't spread too wide. Stays readable even on big monitors.

Grid.desc: A way to arrange items in rows and columns. Say "3-column grid" and you get three across.

Card.cap: A box holding one bundle of info
Card.desc: A photo, title, and description grouped in one box. A border or shadow sets it apart.

Card Grid.cap: Cards lined up in a grid
Card Grid.desc: Several cards laid out in neat rows. Common for product lists and portfolios.

Table.desc: Data of the same kind organized in rows and columns. Great for things like an applicant list.

Tabs.cap: Menu that swaps just the content
Tabs.desc: A menu that swaps content in the same spot. Switches views without loading a new page.

Hamburger Menu.desc: The three-line button that hides the menu on mobile. Tap it and the menu unfolds.

Drawer.cap: Menu panel that slides in from the side
Drawer.desc: A panel that slides in from the screen's edge. Tapping a hamburger menu usually opens one.

Dropdown Menu.cap: Menu that unfolds below a button
Dropdown Menu.desc: A list that drops down when you tap a button. Like a select, but also used for action menus.

Kebab / Overflow Menu.desc: A menu that hides rarely used actions behind three dots. Usually where Edit and Delete live.

Accordion.cap: List that expands and collapses on tap
Accordion.desc: Tap a heading to expand its content; tap again to collapse it. Perfect for FAQs.

Breadcrumb.desc: Shows where you are as a path. Makes it easy to jump back up a level.

Pagination.desc: Splits a long list into pages you hop between by number. Common on forums and message boards.

Stepper.desc: Shows which step you're on out of several. Used in signup flows and checkout.

Bottom Tab Bar.cap: Icon menu row at the bottom of a phone
Bottom Tab Bar.desc: Icon menu pinned to the bottom of an app. Usually 3 to 5 items, easy to reach with a thumb.

Carousel.desc: A set of slides you flip through sideways. The dots below (●○○) show which one you're on.

Filter / Sort.cap: Narrow the list and change its order
Filter / Sort.desc: Filter keeps only what matches; sort changes the order. Both usually sit together above a list.

Button.cap: Anything you press is a button
Button.desc: Something happens when you press it. Shape doesn't matter: if you press it, it's a button.

Primary.cap: Solid fill · only one per screen
Primary.desc: The most important button. Solid color so it stands out, and only one per screen.

Secondary.desc: The second choice, placed next to the primary. Just an outline, so it stands out less.

Ghost / Text.desc: Text-only button, no background or border. For optional actions like Cancel or Skip.

Destructive.cap: Red only for things you can't undo
Destructive.desc: Red button for actions you can't undo, like Delete. Use red everywhere and it loses its punch.

CTA.cap: The one action that matters most
CTA.desc: Call To Action. The one thing you want people to do on this page: sign up, buy, get started.

Icon Button.desc: A button with only an icon, no label. Use when the meaning is obvious: close, like, share.

FAB.cap: Round button floating in a corner
FAB.desc: Round button that floats in a corner even as you scroll. Save it for one frequent action.

Link.cap: Not a button, a text link
Link.desc: Text that jumps you somewhere else when clicked. Usually underlined or a different color.

Button Group.desc: Related buttons joined together in one row. Often used for switching between views.

Social Login.cap: Kakao yellow, Naver green, Google white
Social Login.desc: One-tap login with another service's account, in its brand colors. Kakao and Naver are Korean.

Chat Widget.desc: Floating support button that opens a chat. Kakao Channel and Channel Talk are common in Korea.

Form.cap: Input fields and a button, together
Form.desc: A group of fields that collects user info. Applications, inquiries, and logins are all forms.

Input.cap: A single line for typing text
Input.desc: A one-line text field. For short things like a name, email, or phone number.

Textarea.cap: A big box for several lines
Textarea.desc: A larger box for typing several lines. Used for inquiry messages and short bios.

Search Bar.desc: An input field for search terms. Comes with a magnifying-glass icon.

Autocomplete.cap: Suggestions pop up as you type
Autocomplete.desc: Type a few letters and matching suggestions appear. Great for search boxes and address fields.

Select.desc: A field you click to open a list and pick one option. Also called a dropdown.

Checkbox.desc: Little squares you check to make a choice. You can pick as many as you like at once.

Radio.desc: Round buttons where only one can be on. Pick a new one and the old one turns off.

Toggle.desc: An on/off switch that applies instantly. This page's dark mode switch, top right, is one.

Slider.desc: Drag the handle to set a value. Common for price ranges and volume.

Number Stepper.desc: Plus and minus buttons that adjust a number. You see it a lot for cart quantities.

Rating.desc: Score something by how many stars you give it. Used for reviews.

Color Picker.desc: A tool for choosing a color. A code like #E1785C is more precise than saying "orange."

Date Picker.cap: Pick a date on a calendar
Date Picker.desc: Opens a calendar so you can click a date. Fewer mistakes than typing it in by hand.

Time Picker.desc: Lets you choose hours and minutes. Used for bookings and reminders.

OTP Input.cap: Jumps to the next box on its own
OTP Input.desc: One box per digit of the verification code texted to you. Fill one and it hops to the next.

Tag Input.cap: Press Enter to turn words into chips
Tag Input.desc: A field where each word you add becomes a chip. Used for interests and keywords.

File Upload.desc: An area for adding files. Click to choose one or drag it in.

Drag and Drop.cap: Grab it, move it, drop it
Drag and Drop.desc: Grab an item with the mouse and drop it where you want. Used for reordering and file uploads.

Label.desc: The name tag that says what goes in a field. A red star means it's required.

Placeholder.desc: The faint example text inside a field. It disappears once you start typing.

Helper Text.desc: The small note under a field. It tells you the rules or gives a hint before you type.

Validation.cap: Checks that the format is right
Validation.desc: Checks whether what you typed follows the rules. Mistakes turn red right away.

Submit.desc: Sending what you filled in to the server. The "Send" button is the submit button.

Terms Agreement.desc: Checkboxes to accept terms all at once or one by one. Korean sites split required vs. optional.

Identity Verification.cap: Pick your carrier → verify by phone
Identity Verification.desc: Phone-based check that you're really you. A common step when signing up for Korean services.

Address Search.desc: Search a zip code and the address auto-fills. You only type the unit number. Common in Korea.

Default.desc: How it looks before anyone touches it. Every other state starts from here.

Hover.cap: When the mouse is over it
Hover.desc: A slight change when the mouse is over it, hinting it's clickable. Phones don't have hover.

Active / Pressed.desc: How it looks the instant you press it. Gives a slightly pushed-in feel.

Focus.desc: An outline showing where you are as you Tab through a page. A must for accessibility.

Disabled.cap: Grayed out so you can't press it
Disabled.desc: Can't be pressed because some condition isn't met yet. Shown grayed out and faded.

Loading.desc: While the server works on it. Blocks a second press and shows a spinner in the meantime.

Selected.desc: The one picked out of several. A filled-in color sets it apart.

Error / Invalid.desc: When what you typed is wrong. Shows a red outline along with the reason why.

Success.desc: When things went right. Shows a green check mark to confirm.

Read-only.desc: You can see the value but not change it. Unlike disabled, you can still copy it.

Badge.desc: A tiny number or dot pinned to the corner of an icon. Think unread notification counts.

Status Dot.cap: A dot whose color shows status
Status Dot.desc: A single colored dot that tells you the status. Green means online, gray means offline.

Chip.cap: Often tapped to filter a list
Chip.desc: A small pill-shaped label, also called a tag. Often a filter; an ✕ means you can remove it.

Kbd.desc: Keyboard shortcuts drawn to look like real keys. Used in docs and help pages.

Avatar.cap: First initial when there's no photo
Avatar.desc: A round photo that stands for a person. No photo? It shows the first letter of their name.

Avatar Group.desc: Several avatars overlapping each other. Used to show "these people are taking part."

Divider.desc: A thin line between chunks of content. Use it when white space alone isn't enough.

Icon.desc: A small picture that stands for a meaning. Name a set like Lucide so they all match in style.

Modal / Dialog.desc: A window in the middle that blocks the page until you close it. Save it for big confirmations.

Overlay.desc: The dark, see-through layer behind a modal. It pulls your eyes to what's in front.

Bottom Sheet.desc: A panel that slides up from the bottom of the screen. A popular stand-in for modals on mobile.

Confirmation.cap: A window that asks "Are you sure?"
Confirmation.desc: A window that double-checks before an action you can't easily undo. It's a kind of modal.

Toast.desc: A quick message that pops up at the top or bottom, then fades on its own. Like "Saved!"

Alert.desc: A message strip built into the page. Green means success, yellow caution, red error.

Field Error.desc: Error text right under the wrong field. It shows exactly what to fix, so it beats an alert.

Cookie Banner.desc: A strip asking permission to use cookies. You'll need one if you have visitors from Europe.

Tooltip.cap: Small note that appears on hover
Tooltip.desc: A short note in a bubble that shows when you hover your mouse. It vanishes when you move away.

Popover.cap: Small panel you click to open
Popover.desc: A small panel that opens when you click. Bigger than a tooltip, and it can hold buttons.

Progress Bar.cap: Bar showing how far along you are
Progress Bar.desc: A bar that fills up to show progress. Use it when you know how long the wait will be.

Spinner.desc: A spinning loading sign. Use it when you don't know how long the wait will be.

Skeleton.cap: Gray shapes where content will load
Skeleton.desc: Gray blocks that hold the spot until content arrives. Feels less stuck than a spinner.

Empty State.desc: The screen you see when there's nothing yet. Don't leave it blank; suggest what to do next.

Promo Popup.desc: A promo window that pops up the moment you arrive. Always add a "Don't show today" option.

App Install Banner.cap: "Open in app" strip at the top
App Install Banner.desc: A strip on mobile web nudging you to install the app. Once closed, it shouldn't come back.

Share Sheet.desc: The panel that slides up when you tap Share. It's a kind of bottom sheet.

List.desc: Items of the same shape stacked top to bottom. Think post lists or sign-up lists.

Timeline.cap: Events lined up in time order
Timeline.desc: Events pinned to a vertical line in time order. Good for progress steps or company history.

Notification.desc: A list of new updates, newest first. Unread ones get a little dot.

Gallery.cap: Photos laid out in a grid
Gallery.desc: Photos arranged in a grid. Great for portfolios and product shots.

Lightbox.desc: Tap a photo and it opens big, filling the screen. Goes hand in hand with a gallery.

Stats.desc: Numbers worth bragging about, shown big. Three is the sweet spot.

Stat Card.desc: A card with one number plus how much it changed. A dashboard staple.

Pricing Table.desc: Plans lined up side by side so people can compare. Mark the one you recommend as "Popular."

Testimonial.desc: A quote from a real user. Adding a name and company makes it more believable.

Logo Cloud.desc: Logos of companies that use your product, shown in gray. It's there to build trust.

Profile Card.desc: A card about a person: avatar, name, one-line bio, and a button.

Blockquote.cap: Quoted paragraph with a left bar
Blockquote.desc: Someone else's words or a line worth highlighting, set apart with a bar on the left.

Code Block.cap: Box that shows code as is
Code Block.desc: A dark box that shows code or commands in a monospace font. Pair it with a copy button.

Banner.cap: Notice strip stuck to the top
Banner.desc: A notice strip stuck to the top of the page. Always give it a close button.

FAQ.cap: Tap a question to reveal the answer
FAQ.desc: Common questions collected in an accordion. Cuts down on support requests.

Feature Grid.cap: Icon, title, and blurb, three across
Feature Grid.desc: Three or so icon + title + one-liner blocks in a row. A landing page staple.

How It Works.desc: Shows how to use something in three steps. The numbered circles are the signature touch.

Comparison Table.desc: Compares features against competitors with ✓ and ✕. Highlight your own column.

Table of Contents.cap: List of headings, tap to jump
Table of Contents.desc: A list of a long article's headings. Tap one to jump straight to that section.

Newsletter Signup.cap: Email field + subscribe button, one row
Newsletter Signup.desc: A short form that asks for just an email. Put it in the footer or at the end of a post.

Countdown.cap: Numbers ticking down to a deadline
Countdown.desc: Shows the time left until a deadline, live. Used for events and early-bird deals.

Video Embed.cap: YouTube video dropped into the page
Video Embed.desc: Puts a YouTube-style video right on the page. All you need is the link.

Team Section.cap: Grid of team photos, names, and titles
Team Section.desc: Shows the people behind the product with photos, names, and roles. Builds trust.

Product Card.desc: One product per card: photo, name, price, star rating. The basic unit of any shop listing.

Discount Price.cap: Old price crossed out, % off in red
Discount Price.desc: Crosses out the original price, then shows the percent off and the real price. Percent in red.

Coupon.cap: Coupon shape with a dotted tear line
Coupon.desc: A card styled to look like a real paper coupon. The dotted tear-off line is the key detail.

Wishlist.cap: Tap ♡ to save, it fills in as ♥
Wishlist.desc: A heart button for saving things you like. Tap it and the heart fills in.

Review Card.desc: One buyer's star rating, review, and photo in a card. The shopping version of a testimonial.

Rating Breakdown.cap: Bars for how many gave 5, 4, 3 stars
Rating Breakdown.desc: Bars showing where the star ratings cluster, from 5 down to 1. Sits next to the average score.

Sticky Bottom Bar.desc: A row of buy buttons glued to the bottom as you scroll. A must on product detail pages.

Responsive.cap: More columns as the screen gets wider
Responsive.desc: Layout adapts to the screen: one column on phones, three on desktop. This page does it too.

Mobile First.cap: Instagram visitors are all on phones
Mobile First.desc: Build for phones first, then widen for desktop. Go the other way and it breaks on phones.

Breakpoint.cap: The width where the layout switches
Breakpoint.desc: The screen width where the layout changes. 768px and 1024px are the usual ones.

Sticky.cap: Header stays at the top as you scroll
Sticky.desc: Snaps to the top and follows you as you scroll. The header on this page is sticky.

Fixed.cap: Pinned to the screen, scroll or not
Fixed.desc: Always in the same spot no matter how far you scroll. Think floating buttons and chat icons.

Margin.desc: The empty space outside an element. It sets how far it sits from its neighbors.

Padding.desc: The empty space inside an element. Breathing room between the border and the text.

Gap / Spacing.desc: The distance between side-by-side elements. In a grid, one gap value handles them all.

Border Radius.desc: How rounded a box's corners are. Set it to 999px and it becomes a full circle.

Box Shadow.desc: A shadow under an element that makes it look like it's floating. Subtle usually looks best.

Dark Mode.desc: A flipped theme: dark background, light text. Try the switch at the top right of this page.

Opacity.desc: How see-through something is. 100% is solid, 0% is invisible. Use it to fade things out.

Border.desc: The line around an element. You set its thickness, color, and whether it's solid or dashed.

Gradient.cap: A background that slowly shifts color
Gradient.desc: A background that blends from one color into another. You can pick the direction too.

Aspect Ratio.desc: Width-to-height ratio. Say "make the photo box 16:9" and it keeps its shape at any size.

Fade In.desc: Starts invisible and slowly comes into view. About 0.6 seconds feels natural.

Scroll Reveal.cap: Appears as it scrolls into view
Scroll Reveal.desc: Things appear as you scroll them into view. The cards on this page do exactly that.

Transition.desc: When something changes, it moves smoothly instead of snapping. 0.2 seconds is plenty.

Alignment.desc: Which side text or elements line up to. Just say "center it" or "align it left."

Centering.cap: Dead center, both across and down
Centering.desc: Placing something in the exact middle, both across and down. Say "dead center of the screen."

Horizontal Scroll.cap: A list you swipe sideways to browse
Horizontal Scroll.desc: Cards line up side by side and you swipe across to see more. Very common on mobile.

Overflow.cap: Content spilling out of its box
Overflow.desc: When content is bigger than its box and pokes out. You either hide it or make it scroll.

z-index.cap: Which layer sits on top or underneath
z-index.desc: Decides what shows on top when elements overlap. The higher the number, the higher it sits.

Font Size.desc: How big the text is. Body text is usually 16px, and never below 14px on phones.

Font Weight.desc: How thick the letters are. 400 is regular, 700 is bold. Using numbers keeps it precise.

Hierarchy.desc: Heading, subheading, and body text step down in size and weight so the eye knows where to go.

Ellipsis.desc: Text too long for its box gets cut to "…" so it fits on one line. Common in title lists.

Line Break.cap: Keeps words from breaking in half
Line Break.desc: Keeps a word from being split when text wraps to a new line. Say "wrap by whole words."

layout.desc: The big bones of a screen. Words for where things sit.

nav.desc: Getting around. Words for how you move from here to there.

button.desc: Things you press. The look changes with importance.

form.desc: Fields that collect info. Signup, contact, login: all forms.

state.desc: One button, many looks. Say "make it darker on hover."

element.desc: Tiny bits all over the screen. Just say "add a badge here."

feedback.desc: Things that say what happened, or cover the screen.

content.desc: Blocks that hold content. Mix these to build a landing page.

commerce.desc: Online store parts. Show one product, get it bought.

concept.desc: Not parts, but words you'll need: size, space, motion.
